@@ -0,0 +1,30 @@
+---
+assignees:
+- claude-code
+depends_on:
+- 01M4R0ANACQ08YDG539AAJ8FA4
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: '8180'
+title: 'read resource: give the absolute path of a binary file, not an error'
+---
+## What
+Now, `read resource` of a file that is not UTF-8 text (for example `assets/logo.bin`) gives a corrective message (`ReadResource.nonUTF8Message`). Change this to a successful result. The result tells the model that the file is binary, and it gives the absolute path of the winning copy and the byte size. The model can then give the path to a different tool that can use binary files.
+
+- `Sources/FoundationModelsSkills/Resources/ResourceRow.swift`: change `ReadResourceResult` so that it can also show a binary file. Add these fields: `binary: Bool`, `absolutePath: String?` and `byteSize: Int?`. For a text read, `binary` is `false` and the two new fields are `nil`, so the JSON of a text read keeps its fields. For a binary read, `content` is one sentence, for example: "This file is binary. It is not shown as text. Its absolute path is `<path>` and its size is <n> bytes." `start`, `end` and `totalLines` are `0` for a binary read. Update the `init` and the doc comments.
+- `Sources/FoundationModelsSkills/Resources/ReadResource.swift`: in `execute(in:)`, the `.nonUTF8` case of the scan returns `.success` with the binary result. The absolute path is `overlay.resolve(relativePath)?.url` with symlinks resolved (`.resolvingSymlinksInPath().path`). The `path` field is the relative path. The scan still stops at the first byte that is not valid UTF-8, thus the operation never loads the whole binary file. Delete `nonUTF8Message`. Update the doc comments that name the non-UTF-8 corrective.
+- `ReadResource.operationDescription`: add that a binary file gives its absolute path and its size, not its content.
+- `docs/operations.md`: in the `read resource` row, say what a binary file gives.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] `read resource` of `assets/logo.bin` in the `release-notes` fixture gives `.success` with `binary == true`, the correct `byteSize`, an `absolutePath` that is the winning copy on the disk, and a `content` sentence that says the file is binary.
+- [ ] The absolute path that the result gives, when used as the `path` of a second `read resource` call, gives the same binary result again. This makes sure that it works with the absolute-path rule.
+- [ ] A text read gives the same JSON fields and values as now, with `binary: false`.
+- [ ] A binary copy in a lower layer, with no copy in a higher layer, gives the absolute path of the lower-layer copy.
+
+## Tests
+- [ ] `Tests/FoundationModelsSkillsTests/ReadResourceTests.swift`: change the non-UTF-8 corrective test to the binary-success test, add the absolute-path round-trip test, and add the lower-layer binary test.
+- [ ] `Tests/FoundationModelsSkillsTests/ResourceOpsTests.swift`, and each other test that expects the non-UTF-8 corrective (search for `not valid UTF-8`): update it to the new result.
+- [ ] `swift test` passes with no failure.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write failing tests first, then implement to make them pass.
\ No newline at end of file
